```python
def pluck(arr):
    """
    Given an array representing a branch of a tree that has non-negative integer nodes,
    pluck the node with the smallest even value and return it as [value, index].
    If several nodes share the smallest even value, return the one with the smallest index.
    If there are no even values or the array is empty, return [].
    """
    best_val, best_idx = None, -1
    for i, v in enumerate(arr):
        if v % 2 == 0 and (best_val is None or v < best_val):
            best_val, best_idx = v, i
    return [] if best_val is None else [best_val, best_idx]
```

This makes one pass over the array, so it runs in O(n) time and O(1) extra space. Because it uses strict `<`, the first occurrence wins when values tie, which gives the smallest index.
